name: a-shared-file-still-stops-the-merge
breaks: the disjointness saving added in #1323 inverts: a change that touches the very files main just changed is merged without being run against them, which is the one case the behind-main refusal exists for, while a change that touches nothing in common is refused instead. Measured on 2026-09-04, 32 of 41 merges that day shared a file, so this is the common case rather than the edge
